record.title: Sprung contact — a formed spring finger bearing on a cell face, with the door supplying the clamp
record.why: The GEOMETRY is measured: three fingers, dimples touching the cell's faces at z=4.042 with zero interference, at R9.50 (two, positive) and R6.00 (one, negative). The FORCE IS CALCULATED, NOT MEASURED — k = 3EI/L^3 = 1.4912 N/mm on the modelled L=6.074, w=3.60, t=0.15 in C5191, giving 0.596 N per finger at the 0.400 mm working deflection. w/L = 0.59, so the strip behaves partly as a plate and the real rate is up to 12 percent higher. Contact resistance has not been measured at all. A force gauge and a milliohm meter on stamped samples settle both.

joins.a: a stamped spring finger, insert-moulded into a carrier, drawn at its compressed height
joins.b: a coin cell's positive can rim or negative face

dof_left: tz within the finger's working travel
record.adds_parts_why: this joint consumes no part; it joins two. No fastener, and deliberately so — a screw would cost 1.5-2.5 mm of a 7.98 mm budget and put metal inside Apple's Ø37.31 antenna keep-out (DECISIONS.md D13).
record.standard_why: No contact-resistance or contact-force standard was fetched. The 0.5-1.5 N band this folder designs to is common practice, not a cited requirement.
